items.label: Honeywell Aerospace Q2 FY2026 (08-05-2026)
items.signal_prefix: CFO Josh Jepsen (first earnings call after the spin-off from

set.signal: CFO Josh Jepsen (first earnings call after the spin-off from Honeywell completed on June 29, per CEO Jim Currier; he said he discussed profit metrics on a pro forma standalone basis, as if the company had been operating independently for the full quarter and comparable period): Q2 sales increased 5% organically to $4.5 billion; adjusted EBIT was $1 billion, down 2% on unfavorable mix and an inventory obsolescence charge of approximately $50 million (excluding the charge adjusted EBIT would have grown 3%); adjusted EPS was $1.78 (pro forma standalone basis), down on higher taxes and lower adjusted EBIT. Supply constraints shifted shipments to domestic defense and Engines & Power Systems OE, which have lower than group average margins; the obsolescence charge was mostly in Engines & Power Systems and is not expected to recur.
set.figure: Q2 sales $4.5 billion (+5% organic); pro forma standalone adjusted EBIT $1 billion (-2%) and adjusted EPS $1.78; approximately $50 million inventory obsolescence charge

items.reason: Not a transcription error: the CFO stated the call's profit metrics are pro forma standalone (call EBIT -2% vs the same-day release's reported adjusted EBIT -7%); the release prints adjusted EPS $1.87 on the reported adjusted basis (on the Honeywell Aerospace 8-K (08-05-2026) entry). Keep $1.78, state its basis.
items.evidence: I'll discuss our profit metrics on a pro forma standalone basis as if we had been operating independently for the full quarter and comparable period
